questions.prompt: For you are not such a man, Catiline, that either shame ever called you back from disgrace, or fear from danger, or reason from madness.
questions.answer: Neque enim is es, Catilīna, ut tē aut pudor umquam ā turpitūdine, aut metus ā perīculō, aut ratiō ā furōre, revocārit.

questions.prompt: How many thrusts of yours—aimed so that they seemed impossible to avoid—did I escape by a slight swerve and, as they say, with just my body!
questions.answer: Quot ego tuās petītiōnēs — ita coniectās ut vītārī posse nōn vidērentur — parvā quādam dēclīnātiōne et, ut aiunt, corpore effūgī!

questions.prompt: So that Ambiorix might not have a refuge with them.
questions.answer: Nē ad eōs Ambiorīx receptum habēret.

questions.prompt: When these things had been learned, he sends ahead scouts and centurions to choose a place suitable for a camp.
questions.answer: Hīs rēbus cognatis, explōrātōrēs centurionesque praemittit quī locum castrīs idōneum dēligant.

questions.prompt: Nothing is so useful that it is of benefit in passing.
questions.answer: Nihil tam ūtile est ut in trānsitū prōsit.

questions.prompt: When recently, on the death of your former wife, you had emptied your house for a new marriage, did you not also heap this crime upon another unbelievable crime?
questions.answer: Nūper cum morte superiōris uxōris novīs nūptiīs domum vacuēfēcissēs, nōnne etiam aliō incrēdibilī scelere hoc scelus cumulāstī?

questions.prompt: This I pass over and readily allow to be kept silent, lest in this state the enormity of so great a crime should seem either to have existed or to have gone unpunished.
questions.answer: Quod ego praetermittō et facile patior silērī, nē in hāc cīvitāte tantī facinoris immanitās aut exstitisse aut nōn vindicāta esse videātur.

questions.prompt: But you will forgive me; for I have been carried away by my enthusiasm for country matters, and old age is by nature rather talkative — so that I may not seem to be clearing it of every fault.
questions.answer: Ignōscētis autem; nam et studiō rūsticārum rērum prōvectus sum, et senectūs est nātūra loquācior — nē ab omnibus eam vitiīs videar vindicāre.

questions.prompt: And so, in order to get away more quickly, I steered straight out through the open sea to Nesis, intending to cut off all the bends.
questions.answer: Itaque quō celerius ēvāderem, prōtinus per altum ad Nēsida dērēxī praecīsūrus omnēs sinūs.

questions.prompt: And so, when the parents of one crucified man saw that the guard had been relaxed, they took him down as he hung by night and committed him to his last rites.
questions.answer: Itaque ūnī̆us cruciāriī parentēs ut vīdērunt laxātam custōdiam, dētrāxēre nocte pendentem supremoque mandāvērunt officiō.

questions.prompt: They brought Cincinnatus from the plough that he might be dictator.
questions.answer: Ab arātrō abdūxērunt Cincinnātum, ut dictātor esset.

questions.prompt: For this reason we are subject to the laws, that we may be free.
questions.answer: Lēgum idcircō servī sumus, ut līberī sīmus.

questions.prompt: Lucius Decidius Saxa is sent to examine the ground.
questions.answer: Mittitur L. Dēcidius Saxa quī locī nātūram perspiciat.

questions.prompt: He wrote speeches for other men to deliver.
questions.answer: Scrībēbat ōrātiōnēs quās aliī dīcerent.

questions.prompt: You have left him no ground even to make a stand against you.
questions.answer: Huic nē ubi cōnsisteret quidem contrā tē locum relīquistī.

questions.prompt: He took advantage of liberty, that he might bluster with more impunity.
questions.answer: Lībertāte ūsus est, quō impūnius dicāx esset.

questions.prompt: Lucius Sulla had treated the army luxuriously, in order to make it devoted to him.
questions.answer: L. Sulla exercitum, quō sibi fīdum faceret, lūxuriōsē habuerat.

questions.prompt: But, to return to the same point, this was the cause of fear.
questions.answer: Sed ut eōdem revertar, causa haec fuit timōris.

questions.prompt: It was the act of one rash enough, not to say daring.
questions.answer: Satis incōnsīderātī fuit, nē dīcam audācis.

questions.prompt: For prosperity overmasters the soul even of the wise; much less did they with their corrupt morals put any check on victory.
questions.answer: Quippe secundae rēs sapientium animōs fatīgant; nē illī corruptīs mōribus victōriae temperārent.

questions.prompt: Such an outcry was made in the senate-house that the people hurried together.
questions.answer: Tantus in cūriā clāmor factus est ut populus concurreret.

questions.prompt: They say many things which I hardly understand.
questions.answer: Multa dīcunt quae vix intellegam.

questions.prompt: We must always aim at a peace which shall have no plots.
questions.answer: Quae nihil habitūra sit īnsidiārum semper est cōnsulendum.

questions.prompt: There are some who think that the departure of soul from body constitutes death.
questions.answer: Sunt quī discessum animī ā corpore putent esse mortem.

questions.prompt: There were some who pitied Helvidius.
questions.answer: Erant quī Helvidium miserārentur.

questions.prompt: I see nothing to fear.
questions.answer: Nihil videō quod timeam.

questions.prompt: There is no reason why you should dread my coming.
questions.answer: Nihil est quod adventum nostrum extimēscās.

questions.prompt: There was nothing left from which an embankment could be got together.
questions.answer: Unde agger comportārī posset nihil erat reliquum.

questions.prompt: There are certain animals in which there is something like virtue.
questions.answer: Sunt bēstiae quaedam in quibus inest aliquid simile virtūtis.

questions.prompt: Many were found of such a character as to be ready to give their lives for their country.
questions.answer: Inventī multī sunt quī vītam prōfundere prō patriā parātī essent.

questions.prompt: I seem to myself to have done wrong because I have left you.
questions.answer: Peccāsse mihi videor quī ā tē discesserim.

questions.prompt: O guileless man, who hides nothing from us!
questions.answer: Virum simplicem quī nōs nihil cēlet!

questions.prompt: Nor did the consul delay the fight, since he had sought that very thing. as who had sought.
questions.answer: Nec cōnsul, ut quī id ipsum quaesīsset, moram certāminī fēcit.

questions.prompt: There is sharp fighting in the rear, so that they almost take flight.
questions.answer: Pūgnātur ācriter ad novissimum agmen, adeō ut paene terga convertant.

questions.prompt: Who went to sea who did not incur the peril of death?
questions.answer: Quis nāvigāvit quī nōn sē mortis perīculō committeret?

questions.prompt: Nobody is so old as not to think that he can live a year.
questions.answer: Nēmō est tam senex quī sē annum nōn putet posse vīvere.

questions.prompt: This is so far useful that we are not utterly mocked by the accusers useful only on this condition, that.
questions.answer: Hōc ita est ūtile ut nē plānē inlūdāmur ab accūsātōribus.

questions.prompt: But nothing is troublesome which you do not miss.
questions.answer: Nihil autem est molestum quod nōn dēsīderēs.

questions.prompt: Why then do I not wish for peace? Because it is disgraceful.
questions.answer: Cūr igitur pācem nōlō? Quia turpis est.

questions.prompt: So it happens that they attend because they follow duty, but are silent because they seek to avoid danger.
questions.answer: Ita fit ut adsint proptereā quod officium sequuntur, taceant autem quia periculum vītant.

questions.prompt: Themistocles used to walk about at night because he could not sleep.
questions.answer: Noctū ambulābat Themistoclēs quod somnum capere nōn posset.

questions.prompt: Boxers groan, not because they are in pain, but because by giving vent to the voice the whole body is put in a state of tension.
questions.answer: Pugilēs ingemēscunt, nōn quod doleant, sed quia profundendā vōce omne corpus intenditur.

questions.prompt: I must review the point, since Murena has so wished.
questions.answer: Locus est ā mē, quoniam ita Murēna voluit, retrāctandus.

questions.prompt: When the soldiers had won the victory, they left nothing to the vanquished.
questions.answer: Mīlitēs postquam victōriam adeptī sunt, nihil reliquī victīs fēcēre.

questions.prompt: When he understood that all agreed he appointed the next day for the battle.
questions.answer: Ubi omnīs idem sentīre intellēxit, posterum diem pūgnae cōnstituit.

questions.prompt: When Catiline sees that they have come together, he retires.
questions.answer: Catilīna, ubi eōs convēnisse videt, sēcēdit.

questions.prompt: Our men, as soon as they had taken a position on dry ground, made an attack on the enemy.
questions.answer: Nostrī simul in āridō cōnstitērunt, in hostīs impetum fēcērunt.

questions.prompt: When they stood in array on both sides, the generals advance into the midst.
questions.answer: Postquam strūctī utrimque stābant, ducēs in medium prōcēdunt.

questions.prompt: When I was trying to force him from the city, I looked forward to this.
questions.answer: Quem quidem cum ex urbe pellēbam, hōc prōvidēbam animō.

questions.prompt: When I was taking my ease in my house at Tusculum, I received your letter.
questions.answer: Cum essem ōtiōsus in Tusculānō, accēpī tuās litterās.

questions.prompt: After remaining at Cybistra for five days, I freed King Ariobarzanes from plots.
questions.answer: Cum ad Cybistra quīnque diēs essem morātus, rēgem Ariobarzānem īnsidiīs līberāvī.

questions.prompt: Ten days had not yet passed, when the other infant son was killed.
questions.answer: Diēs nōndum decem intercesserant, cum ille alter fīlius īnfāns necātur.

questions.prompt: They were preparing to do this by night, when the women suddenly ran out into the streets.
questions.answer: Hōc facere noctū apparābant, cum mātrēs familiae repente in pūblicum prōcurrērunt.

questions.prompt: Times occur when those things which seem especially worthy of the upright man, become the opposite.
questions.answer: Incidunt tempora, cum ea, quae maximē videntur dīgna esse iūstō homine, fīunt contrāria.

questions.prompt: I shall not hesitate to take pains to see you, when I can do it conveniently.
questions.answer: Nōn dubitābō dare operam ut tē videam, cum id satis commodē facere poterō.

questions.prompt: This is not difficult since we are so strong in cavalry.
questions.answer: Id difficile nōn est, cum tantum equitātū valeāmus.

questions.prompt: Since solitude is full of treachery and fear, reason itself prompts us to contract friendships.
questions.answer: Cum sōlitūdō īnsidiārum et metūs plēna sit, ratiō ipsa monet amīcitiās comparāre.

questions.prompt: Though the first ranks had fallen, still the others resisted vigorously.
questions.answer: Cum prīmī ōrdinēs concidissent, tamen ācerrimē reliquī resistēbant.

questions.prompt: In a short time he had filled out the legions with their complement of men, though at the start he had not had more than two thousand.
questions.answer: Brevī spatiō legiōnēs numerō hominum explēverat, cum initiō nōn amplius duōbus mīlibus habuisset.

questions.prompt: I find no fault; since I myself did not escape that blame.
questions.answer: Nec reprehendō: quippe cum ipse istam reprehēnsiōnem nōn fūgerim.

questions.prompt: There was not one of the soldiers who was not wounded.
questions.answer: Nēmō fuit mīlitum quīn vulnerārētur.

questions.prompt: Was there any one who did not shed tears?
questions.answer: Ecquis fuit quīn lacrimāret?
